papers.what_it_is: A Quantum Computing Inc resource-library web page listing its featured publications with abstracts, dates and links, not a paper.

assertions.value: The page is a Quantum Computing Inc resource-library listing titled Featured Publications. Each entry gives a title, a short abstract or excerpt, and a date, and most give a link.
assertions.anchor: Page header and entries
quotes: Featured Publications - Quantum Computing Inc Products & services
Featured Publications Zeno Blockade Enabling Photonic Quantum Optimization
assertions.certainty_reason: The page's own header and entry layout state what it is.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstracts are the authors' summaries relayed by the vendor; the page holds no methods, data or proofs, so every result here is second-hand and is graded low.

assertions.value: The authors of the entry dated April 14, 2026 (arXiv 2604.13032) explore an optical quantum optimizer built on non-linear optics that uses Zeno effects to enforce independence constraints and a linear protocol to find a weighted maximum independent set. They report numerical study of the protocol, finding that the coherent form of the Zeno effect performs better than the incoherent form.
assertions.anchor: Entry 1, Zeno Blockade Enabling Photonic Quantum Optimization
quotes: In this work we explore the potential of implementing an optical quantum optimizer using non-linear optics, specifically using sum-frequency generation and/or two photon absorption.
This proposal uses Zeno effects to enforce independence constraints and then a linear protocol to find a maximum independent set in a way where the elements of the set can be weighted.
We numerically study aspects of the protocol, including the effect of coherent versus incoherent incarnations of the Zeno effect, finding superior performance from the former.
April 14, 2026 https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13032
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract relayed by a vendor page; a numerical study with no data on the page.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a proposal with simulation, not a built device; the page gives no problem sizes or numbers.

assertions.value: The authors of the April 14, 2026 entry state that their proposal can be viewed as an implementation of the entropy computing paradigm that uses real rather than imaginary time evolution, or as quantum annealing within a Zeno constrained subspace.
assertions.anchor: Entry 1, Zeno Blockade Enabling Photonic Quantum Optimization
quotes: Our proposal can either be viewed as an implementation of the entropy computing paradigm presented in [Nguyen et.~al.~Communications Physics 1, 411, 8] which uses real rather than imaginary time evolution, or as quantum annealing within a Zeno constrained subspace.
April 14, 2026
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own framing of their proposal, relayed by a vendor page.

assertions.value: The authors of the entry dated November 30, 2025 (arXiv 2512.00675) report that, for non-negative real matrices, first using Dirac-3 and then passing its results as the initial factor matrices to Scikit-learn's NMF procedure gives a smaller error in the reconstructed matrices than Scikit-learn's NMF procedure with default parameters on its own.
assertions.anchor: Entry 2, Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Using Non-Von Neumann Computers
quotes: we observed that a fusion approach of first using Dirac-3 and then feeding its results as the initial factor matrices to Scikit-learn's NMF procedure
outperforms Scikit-learn's NMF procedure on its own, with default parameters in terms of the error in the reconstructed matrices.
November 30, 2025 https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00675
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one preliminary study, relayed by a vendor page.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract gives no matrix sizes, error values or run counts, so the size of the gain is unknown from this page.

assertions.value: The authors of the November 30, 2025 entry report that on non-negative integer matrices, for serial processing, Dirac-3 outperforms Google's CP-SAT solver (inside the Or-Tools package) in a majority of the cases.
assertions.anchor: Entry 2, Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Using Non-Von Neumann Computers
quotes: we compared the Dirac-3 device to Google's CP-SAT solver (inside the Or-Tools package) and found that for serial processing, Dirac-3 outperforms CP-SAT in a majority of the cases.
November 30, 2025
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one preliminary study, relayed by a vendor page.
assertions.reader_inference: The qualifier is serial processing only; the abstract does not say what happens for parallel processing.

assertions.value: The authors of the November 30, 2025 entry state that current devices cannot solve large NMF problems, that their experiments were preliminary, and that future work may identify domains and variants where entropy computing and other non-von Neumann architectures offer a clear advantage.
assertions.anchor: Entry 2, Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Using Non-Von Neumann Computers
quotes: Although current devices cannot solve large NMF problems, the results of our preliminary experiments are promising enough to warrant further research.
We believe that future work in this area might be able to identify domains and variants of the problem where entropy computing (and other non-von Neumann architectures) could offer a clear advantage.
November 30, 2025
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of a limit, relayed by a vendor page.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors do not claim an advantage has been shown; the last sentence is hedged with 'might' and 'could'.

assertions.value: The authors of the November 30, 2025 entry state that their formulations are a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization model (QUBO, suitable for Ising machines) and a quartic formulation that allows real-valued and integer variables (suitable for machines like the Dirac-3).
assertions.anchor: Entry 2, Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Using Non-Von Neumann Computers
quotes: Our formulations consist of (i) a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization model (QUBO, suitable for Ising machines) and a quartic formulation that allows for real-valued and integer variables (suitable for machines like the Dirac-3).
November 30, 2025
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' statement of their own setup, in the abstract excerpt on the page.

assertions.value: The authors of the entry dated July 5, 2024 report that they experimentally demonstrate the feasibility of entropy computing by building a hybrid photonic-electronic computer that uses optical measurement and feedback to solve non-convex optimization problems, and that temporal photonic modes create qudits that encode probability amplitudes in the time-frequency degree of freedom of a photon.
assertions.anchor: Entry 3, Entropy Computing: A Paradigm for Optimization in an Open Quantum System
quotes: we experimentally demonstrate the feasibility of entropy computing by building a hybrid photonic-electronic computer that uses optical measurement and feedback to solve non-convex optimization problems.
The system functions by using temporal photonic modes to create qudits in order to encode probability amplitudes in the time-frequency degree of freedom of a photon.
July 5, 2024 https://www.nature.com/articles/s42005-025-02324-6
assertions.certainty_reason: A proof-of-principle experiment from one group, relayed by a vendor page.
assertions.reader_inference: The page date (2024) and the journal article id (s42005-025-...) differ; the date likely marks a preprint, but the page does not say so.

assertions.value: The authors of the July 5, 2024 entry state that the entropy computing paradigm can act as a scalable and versatile platform for tackling a large range of NP-hard optimization problems.
assertions.anchor: Entry 3, Entropy Computing: A Paradigm for Optimization in an Open Quantum System
quotes: We show that the proposed entropy computing paradigm can act as a scalable and versatile platform for tackling a large range of NP-hard optimization problems.

This scheme, when coupled with with electronic interconnects, allows us to encode an arbitrary Hamiltonian into the system and solve non-convex continuous variables and combinatorial optimization problems.
July 5, 2024
assertions.certainty_reason: A company-affiliated description of its own paradigm; the page shows no scaling data.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract excerpt gives no problem sizes or scaling measurements, so 'scalable' is not supported by anything on this page.

assertions.value: The authors of the entry dated April 28, 2025 state that their three-state-system construction recovers the dynamics of a transverse field Ising model, and that it implements constraints nonperturbatively without tunable couplers.
assertions.anchor: Entry 4, Zeno-effect computation: Opportunities and challenges
quotes: We find that our model of computing is able to recover the dynamics of a transverse field Ising model.
our methods allow for constraints to be implemented nonperturbatively and do not need tunable couplers, unlike simple transverse field implementations.
April 28, 2025
assertions.certainty_reason: A theoretical result from one group, relayed by a vendor page.

assertions.value: The authors of the April 28, 2025 entry state that settings defined exclusively by measurement or dissipative Zeno effects do not allow for frustration, that pathological spectral features then arise leading to unfavorable runtime scaling, and that adding gain as well as loss, as is often done in an optical setting, is one way to overcome this.
assertions.anchor: Entry 4, Zeno-effect computation: Opportunities and challenges
quotes: We find a substantial challenge that settings defined exclusively by measurement or dissipative Zeno effects do not allow for frustration, and in these settings pathological spectral features arise leading to unfavorable runtime scaling.
We discuss methods to overcome this challenge, for example including gain as well as loss as is often done in an optical setting.
April 28, 2025
assertions.certainty_reason: A limit stated by the authors, relayed by a vendor page.
assertions.reader_inference: This limit bears on the Zeno-based optimizer entries on the same page: a pure measurement or loss Zeno design is reported to have poor runtime scaling.

assertions.value: The authors of the entry dated January 9, 2025 (arXiv 2501.05046) state that they use entropy quantum computing to model and solve the space logistics problem as a time-dependent multicommodity network flow, and that the findings demonstrate suitability for complex interplanetary mission planning.
assertions.anchor: Entry 5, Quantum-Assisted Space Logistics Mission Planning
quotes: This paper leverages entropy quantum computing to model and solve the space logistics problem as a time-dependent multicommodity network flow, enabling the exploration of large solution spaces.
The findings highlight quantum computing's potential to address complex aerospace logistics, demonstrating its suitability for complex interplanetary mission planning.
January 9, 2025 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.05046
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim in an abstract; the page gives no instance sizes, baselines or results.
assertions.reader_inference: 'Demonstrating its suitability' is stronger than the abstract's evidence on this page supports; no comparison with a classical solver appears.

assertions.value: The authors of the entry dated April 27, 2021 report a spectroscope using single-photon counters and a chip-integrated lithium niobate micro-ring filter that samples the atmospheric CO2 absorption spectrum passively at 6 pm resolution by sweeping the filter over 150 pm, and report that the measured absorption near 1572.02 nm agrees well with the transmission spectrum at standard atmospheric pressure.
assertions.anchor: Entry 11, Carbon-dioxide absorption spectroscopy with solar photon counting and integrated lithium niobate micro-ring resonator
quotes: By thermo-optically sweeping the filter over 150 pm and referencing the resulting photon counts to a bypass channel, we sample the absorption spectrum at an ultrahigh-resolution of 6 pm.

we characterize the CO2 absorption through the atmosphere by counting the solar photons across the absorption line around 1572.02 nm, which agrees well with its transmission spectrum at standard atmospheric pressure.
April 27, 2021

assertions.value: The authors of the entry dated March 28, 2023 report that a convolutional neural network, trained end to end on simulated data only, reconstructs two-dimensional images of 32 × 32 pixels of non-line-of-sight targets from 8 × 8 scanning points, a downsampling ratio of 6.25%, and that it works on experimental data.

assertions.value: The authors of the entry dated February 04, 2023 (arXiv 2209.06269) report that a nonlinear optical Ising machine, built from a spatial light modulator, Fourier optics and second-harmonic generation, shows two distinct ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic phase transitions: a second-order transition where the magnetization changes to zero continuously, and a first-order transition where it drops to zero abruptly as the effective temperature increases. They state that a Monte Carlo Metropolis-Hastings simulation corroborates this.
assertions.anchor: Entry 17, Observation of distinct phase transitions in a nonlinear optical Ising machine
quotes: we experimentally observe two distinct ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic phase transitions: a second-order phase transition where the magnetization changes to zero continuously and a first-order phase transition where the magnetization drops to zero abruptly as the effective temperature increases.
Our experimental results are corroborated by a numerical simulation based on the Monte Carlo Metropolis-Hastings algorithm
February 04, 2023 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.06269
assertions.certainty_reason: An experimental result from one study, relayed by a vendor page.
assertions.reader_inference: The arXiv id (2209) points to a 2022 preprint, while the page date is 2023, likely the journal date.
